subject: Privacy & audit playbook request — onboarding Brightline Health
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightlinehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com, security@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: DPIA / audit protocol and Article 28/30 info

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement and our security lead asked me to follow up with a consolidated list of what we need to complete Brightline's vendor onboarding: 

- Canonical Art. 28 processor addendum and any subprocessor flow-down language
- Article 30 processing activities ledger (scope, lawful bases, categories)
- Subprocessor inventory with region and subprocessors' SCCs/adequacy status
- DPIA support notes and any sample exports we can attach to our DPIA
- Audit / inspection protocol: are remote evidence uploads sufficient or do you require on-site audits?

I've attached our standard vendor questionnaire (procurement), but we generally accept evidence bundles / redacted logs. Timeline: procurement is targeting vendor approval by 10/22. Can you confirm what you can provide and by when?

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director, Vendor Risk — Brightline Health
security@brightlinehealth.com

Attachment: brightline-vendor-questionnaire.pdf (pdf stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: DPIA / audit protocol and Article 28/30 info

Hi Daniel — thanks for the checklist and the timeline. Looping in Karthik (privacy), Laura (legal) and Grace (ops) so we can give a consolidated response.

Quick summary of what we can commit to this week: 
- Article 28 addendum: we have a standard DPA exhibit we can share (includes subprocessor flow-down).
- Art 30 ledger: we can provide a scoped processing activities ledger and a short narrative mapping to your DPIA template.
- Subprocessor inventory: we can export current inventory with region mapping and last-assessed dates; we can flag which subprocessors process EU data.
- DPIA support: Karthik can produce a short set of export samples and a walkthrough for your privacy team.
- Audit protocol: remote evidence uploads and targeted log extracts are typically sufficient; we also support scheduled on-site reviews under NDA + reasonable notice.

Can you confirm whether you need SCCs (standard contractual clauses) attached to the subprocessor list or if sufficiency via our contract, DPA and the subprocessors' compliance artifacts is okay?

I'll attach: redwood-article28-30-summary.pdf, dpa-exhibit-subprocessor-list.csv, and a draft dpia-notes doc for your review. If procurement needs DocuSign-ready DPA exhibit, we can prepare one once you confirm the data residency requirements.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-article28-30-summary.pdf, dpa-exhibit-subprocessor-list.csv, dpia-notes-20271012.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: DPIA / audit protocol and Article 28/30 info

Couple of notes on the technical evidence Brightline asked for — suggested mutual action plan below.

Mutual action plan (suggested):
1) By 10/14 — Redwood provides: Art. 28 DPA exhibit, Art. 30 ledger (redacted fields ok), subprocessor CSV with region and last assessment date, SOC 2 Type II (redacted for scope).
2) By 10/18 — Brightline returns any follow-up questions + confirms desired residency constraints (US-only subset / EU residency requirement).
3) By 10/20 — Redwood prepares any scoped exports (redacted) and schedules a 30-min walkthrough with our privacy engineer.

Technical evidence we can share:
- Event-level retention policy and retention schedules per data category
- Example of redacted audit logs (token-level access removed)
- KV-cache prefix policy summary (we do not persist unencrypted customer plaintext beyond configured retention)

On-site audits: we support them under a scoped playbook — we require at least 10 business days notice and a mutual NDA. Remote uploads: preferred for speed; we can create a secure evidence bundle in Drive with time-limited links.

If Brightline requires cross-border specific mitigations (SCCs, SCC+encryption, data localization), we can discuss options — we have EU-region-only deployment plans that can be scoped into Dedicated or Private deployments.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightlinehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com, security@brightlinehealth.com, elaine.hsu@underwriterlegal.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: DPIA / audit protocol and Article 28/30 info

Marissa / team — appreciated. A few clarifications before we proceed: 

- Cross-border transfers: our privacy officer needs explicit confirmation of our options. Do you offer SCCs for processor-subprocessor flows? If not, can you confirm adequacy mechanisms (e.g., EU-region tenancy + no transfer of Brightline EU-personal data to non-adequate jurisdictions)?

- Evidence format: procurement prefers a single Drive evidence bundle + a short checklist we can attach to the DPIA. If you can provide a one-page checklist mapping your artifacts to our DPIA sections that would be ideal.

- Audit rights: Brightline standard language asks for "reasonable audit rights" with a 60-day notice window; can Redwood accept remote audits + an option for an on-site inspection under NDA?

Procurement timeline remains 10/22. Can we confirm the initial bundle by 10/18?

Thanks,
Daniel

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Onboarding: DPIA / audit protocol and Article 28/30 info

Daniel — forwarding a short legal note and the DPA exhibit. A couple of points up front: 

- Redwood accepts remote evidence uploads as the primary mechanism. We will agree to reasonable remote audit rights that are scoped and time-boxed; on-site inspections are permitted only under narrow circumstances (e.g., suspected incident or material breach) and require an NDA and appropriate logistical notice.
- For SCCs: we attach the processor DPA exhibit which references SCCs where required; for subprocessor transfer controls we rely on contractual flow-downs and subprocessors' own adequacy mechanisms. If Brightline requires SCC execution for individual subprocessors, we can discuss a scoped approach.

Please see the attached DPA exhibit (redlined, DocuSign-ready). If procurement needs a version with specific residency-only clauses, flag which data categories and we will escalate to Product for deployment options.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: DPA_Exhibit_REDLINE_for_Brightline.docx (docx stub)
